hints: Transform one string into the other using insert, delete, and replace operations.
Let dp[i][j] be the minimum edits to change the first i characters into the first j characters.
If the last characters match, no new edit is needed; otherwise try each of the three operations.
analogy: Build the target prefix one character at a time, allowing an insertion, removal, or substitution at the end.
example: Changing 'cat' to 'cut' takes one replacement, so the edit distance is 1.
algorithm: Initialize dp[i][0]=i and dp[0][j]=j. For each pair, use dp[i-1][j-1] when characters match; otherwise 1+min(delete, insert, replace).
correctness: The final operation is either unnecessary for equal final characters or one of the three permitted edits; removing that operation gives exactly a smaller prefix problem.
complexity: O(nm) time and O(nm) space, reducible to O(min(n,m)) rows.
